However, the scent is a little medical/non-existent and kind of "old-peoply?" haha I don't know if that makes sense. I just added my own essential oils (lavender, tea tree, lemongrass, chamomile) that help promote good skin and now I have a cream that does good things for my skin and also smells good. It's a good value cause a little goes a long way. Also cetaphil doesn't test on animals so a great choice if you're vegan! Other medical-level creams are nasty w animal cruelty stuff.

title: Perfect for over retinol
review: I've been using Cetaphil Moisturizing Cream on top of my prescription retinol, and it’s been a game-changer for my skincare routine. It’s incredibly moisturizing, soothing any dryness or irritation that sometimes comes with retinoid use. One of the best things about it is that it’s fragrance-free—perfect for sensitive skin—and it hasn't caused any breakouts, which is a huge plus.It's also inexpensive and offers excellent value for money, especially considering how effective it is. The texture is rich but not greasy, and it absorbs well, leaving my skin feeling soft and hydrated.The only downside is the packaging. It comes in a tub, which isn’t the most hygienic or convenient option, especially when you’re trying to use it with clean hands or on the go. A pump bottle would make this product nearly perfect.Overall, highly recommend it if you're looking for a no-frills, dependable moisturizer that plays well with active ingredients.
